title: FUNCTIONAL EMRSs
body_text:
Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that as on date, 508 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) are functional across the country. State and UT-wise status of functional EMRSs is given at Annexure.
In the State of Odisha, 114 EMRSs have been sanctioned out of which 47 EMRSs are functional. None of the blocks in Dhenkanal and Angul districts fulfil the prescribed criteria for establishing EMRS as per existing scheme guidelines.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs informed Lok Sabha that 508 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) are currently functional across India, with state/UT-wise data provided. Odisha has 114 EMRSs sanctioned, of which 47 are functional, while Dhenkanal and Angul districts do not have blocks meeting the scheme's eligibility criteria for setting up new EMRSs. Chhattisgarh (75), Madhya Pradesh (71) and Jharkhand (51) have the highest numbers of functional schools.
enrichment.context:
Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) are a Government of India scheme under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs aimed at providing quality education to Scheduled Tribe (ST) students in remote areas, on par with schools like Navodaya Vidyalayas. As per revised norms, every block with more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons is mandated to have an EMRS by 2022, though implementation has been staggered across states due to infrastructural, land, and administrative constraints. The scheme is fully funded by the central government for infrastructure and shared for recurring costs, and is a key instrument for addressing educational deprivation among tribal communities, complementing other interventions like Ashram Schools and post-matric/pre-matric scholarships for ST students.

The reply highlights persistent gaps between sanctioned and functional schools—a recurring theme in tribal welfare governance, often attributed to delays in land acquisition, faculty recruitment, and construction. The specific mention of Dhenkanal and Angul districts in Odisha not meeting the population/eligibility criteria underscores how the scheme's block-level demographic thresholds determine coverage, leaving certain tribal-populated areas outside its ambit despite genuine need. This ties into broader debates on tribal education policy, the effectiveness of residential schooling models, and disparities in scheme implementation across states with varying tribal populations and administrative capacities.

prelims_questions.question: The Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) scheme is implemented by which of the following ministries?
options: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
prelims_questions.explanation: EMRSs are implemented by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to provide quality residential education to Scheduled Tribe students.

prelims_questions.question: As per the revised norms for Eklavya Model Residential Schools, which of the following blocks are mandated to have an EMRS?
options: Blocks with more than 25% ST population and at least 10,000 tribal persons
Blocks with more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons
Blocks with more than 50% ST population regardless of population size
Blocks with any ST population above 5,000 persons
prelims_questions.explanation: The scheme mandates an EMRS in every block with more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons, as referenced in the context of Odisha's Dhenkanal and Angul districts not meeting this criterion.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the Eklavya Model Residential Schools scheme in addressing educational disparities among Scheduled Tribes in India. What are the challenges in achieving full operationalization of sanctioned schools?

Examine the eligibility criteria for setting up Eklavya Model Residential Schools and analyze whether the current block-level demographic thresholds adequately capture tribal educational needs, especially in states with dispersed tribal populations.
